Headline: Japan’s 2026 Rice Harvest Forecast to Decline 1% to 7.4 MMT
Summary: Japan’s rice production in 2026 is estimated at 7.4 MMT, down 0.8% from 7.5 MMT in 2025, according to the agriculture ministry’s forecast based on crop conditions as of September 25. Despite concerns over prolonged September rainfall, the projected harvest remains relatively high. With supply expected to exceed demand, rice prices could face further downward pressure. Private-sector rice inventories have reached a record high, supported by increased production and government stock releases that began in March 2025.

Headline: Indonesia’s BULOG Records Historic Rice Procurement of 4.1 MMT, Exceeding Target by 2.9%
Summary: Indonesia’s state-owned logistics agency BULOG procured 4.1 MMT of rice equivalent as of October 8, 2026, reaching 102.9% of the government’s 4.0 MMT target under its public service programme. The volume marks a record for the agency, surpassing 3.2 MMT in 2025 and the previous record of 3.7 MMT set in 2012. Higher domestic procurement strengthens the Government Rice Reserve and supports national food security, rice price stabilisation and food assistance programmes. The agency aims to improve stock management, storage and distribution to ensure supplies reach regional markets and meet consumer demand.

Headline: FCI Offers 105,000 Tonnes of Wheat Under OMSS(D); E-Auction Scheduled for October 14
Summary: The Food Corporation of India (FCI) has offered 105,000 metric tonnes of wheat under the Open Market Sale Scheme, Domestic (OMSS(D)), across 22 states and regional entries, covering both Fair Average Quality (FAQ) and Under Relaxed Specifications (URS) categories. The e-auction is scheduled for October 14, 2026. Punjab has the largest allocation at 20,000 tonnes, followed by Haryana and Uttar Pradesh at 9,000 tonnes each, Assam at 8,000 tonnes, Odisha at 7,000 tonnes, and Karnataka at 6,000 tonnes. The listed prices, including reserve prices and transportation costs, range from ₹2,585 per quintal for URS wheat in Haryana to ₹3,043 per quintal in the Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh region. Maharashtra and Goa have price ranges of ₹2,939–₹2,983 per quintal, while Andhra Pradesh ranges from ₹2,878–₹2,943 per quintal. Buyers and traders will assess state-wise delivered costs, transportation expenses, quality specifications, and prevailing local market prices to identify competitive procurement opportunities ahead of the auction.

Headline: Pakistan’s Water Shortage Threatens Wheat Production and Raises Food Price Risks
Summary: Pakistan faces a projected 22% water shortage in Punjab and Sindh during the 2026–27 Rabi season, threatening irrigation supplies for wheat cultivation. Reservoir storage stood at 9.3 million acre-feet on September 30, down from 13.2 million acre-feet a year earlier and below the 10-year average of 9.9 million acre-feet. Wheat flour prices rose 31.7% year-on-year in urban markets and 34.3% in rural areas in September 2026, compared with overall food inflation of 8.2%. Following a previous season’s production shortfall of more than 2 MMT, Pakistan has contracted to import 365,000 tonnes of wheat at $348.83/tonne, with delivery due by November 20. Continued water shortages could reduce yields, increase import dependence, and add pressure to food prices and foreign exchange reserves.

Headline: U.S. Wheat Commercial Sales Fall 32% to 10.1 MMT in 2026/27
Summary: U.S. wheat commercial sales reached 10.1 MMT as of October 1, 2026, down 32% from 14.8 MMT a year earlier. The top 20 destinations accounted for 89% of total sales, compared with 84% last year. Mexico remained the largest buyer at 2.3 MMT (-3%), followed by the Philippines at 1.5 MMT (-5%) and Japan at 1.2 MMT (+4%). Purchases declined sharply in Nigeria (-81% to 0.2 MMT), Indonesia (-62% to 0.3 MMT) and Colombia (-47% to 0.2 MMT), while Bangladesh purchases increased to 0.2 MMT from zero a year earlier. Weekly sales rose by 451,600 tonnes, led by the Philippines (112,000 tonnes), South Korea (100,000 tonnes) and Japan (62,900 tonnes).

Headline: Zimbabwe Tightens Grain Imports to Support Domestic Wheat Production
Summary: Zimbabwe will require grain importers to demonstrate support for local production before receiving import approval, under Statutory Instrument 87 of 2025, while keeping its borders open to grain imports. The country has expanded wheat cultivation from around 60,000 hectares in 2020 to more than 130,000 hectares, with average yields rising from about 2.0 to over 5.3 tonnes per hectare. Despite these gains, Zimbabwe continues to import hard wheat for specific industry requirements. High production costs remain a challenge, with fertiliser accounting for 32–40% of production expenses and most fertiliser supplies imported.

Headline: South Africa’s Wheat Harvest Set to Hit Eight-Year Low Amid Rising Costs and Dry Weather
Summary: South Africa’s wheat production is forecast to decline 5% to 1.8 MMT in 2026/27, its lowest level in eight years, as higher fuel and fertiliser costs and dry conditions in the Western Cape reduce planted area and threaten yields. Overall winter crop production is expected to rise 2% to 2.7 MMT, supported by higher output of barley, canola and oats. Winter crop area reached 851,510 hectares, up 1% year-on-year, with wheat accounting for 57%. Wheat imports are expected to increase to 2.0 MMT from 1.9 MMT in the previous season; although global supplies remain adequate, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruptions and El Niño-related buying could raise import costs.

Headline: Algeria Seeks 50,000 Tonnes of Wheat as Philippine Buyers Purchase 140,000 Tonnes of Feed Wheat
Summary: Algeria’s wheat tender, nominally seeking 50,000 tonnes of milling wheat, closes today, with offers valid until Wednesday. Meanwhile, a Philippine buying group has reportedly purchased around 140,000 tonnes of feed wheat, likely sourced from Australia. These purchases reflect continued import demand from North Africa and Southeast Asia.

Headline: USDA Maintains Kazakhstan’s 2026/27 Wheat Export Forecast at 9.5 MMT
Summary: The USDA kept Kazakhstan’s 2026/27 wheat export forecast unchanged at 9.5 MMT in its October outlook, alongside production at 15.0 MMT and imports at 1.5 MMT. During January– September 2026, rail grain transportation increased 12% year-on-year to 10.8 MMT, including export shipments that rose 14% to 8.4 MMT. Exports to Central Asia increased 33% to 5.5 MMT, with Uzbekistan receiving 4.1 MMT (+44%) and Tajikistan 1.2 MMT (+16%). Shipments to China rose 54% to 750,000 tonnes, while deliveries to Afghanistan surged 4.3-fold to 762,000 tonnes, highlighting expanding regional demand for Kazakhstan’s grain.

Headline: Egypt Procures Nearly 5.0 MMT of Domestic Wheat, Reducing Imports to 12.5 MMT
Summary: Egypt purchased nearly 5.0 MMT of wheat from local farmers during the 2026 procurement season, meeting its government target, while domestic production exceeded 10.0 MMT due to expanded planted area. Higher domestic availability helped reduce wheat imports to 12.5 MMT from 13.2 MMT in the previous fiscal year and strengthened strategic reserves to cover domestic needs for several months. The government aims to limit exposure to global price volatility and international trade disruptions while maintaining supplies for its subsidised baladi bread programme, which serves around 71 million people. Authorities are also expanding digital monitoring of silos, grain movements and stock levels to improve storage efficiency and reduce losses.

Headline: Geopolitical Risks Weigh on Black Sea Grain Supplies as Russian Crop and Export Forecasts Fall
Summary: Geopolitical tensions continued to disrupt grain and energy supply outlooks, with the suspension of US sanctions on Russian diesel and reports of an unconfirmed energy ceasefire adding uncertainty, while Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure threatened refinery capacity and fuel supplies ahead of winter. Efforts by Baltic states to restrict Russian grain transit through Baltic ports added further export-route risks. Russia’s grain crop forecast was cut by 1.0 MMT to 137.0 MMT, while wheat production was lowered by 0.5 MMT to 88.0 MMT. Russian wheat export potential was reduced to 42.0 MMT from 43.5 MMT, with a stress scenario pointing to total grain exports of around 35.0 MMT and the possibility of some crops remaining unharvested until spring.

Headline: NCCF Chana Auction and Sale Updates for 13 October 2026
Summary: NCCF’s Gram sell auction schedule for 13 October covers Rabi-26 Chana stocks across several states, including Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Gujarat, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh. The listed quantities include substantial stocks in Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka, alongside additional lots in Telangana and Gujarat. Separately, the highest approved NCCF PSS bids in Telangana reached ₹10,133/quintal for Tur at Pebbar, while Chana bids stood at ₹7,611 in Pebbar and Doulthabad and ₹7,600 in Sarangpur. The auction schedule indicates continued government-stock availability, while approved bid prices provide a benchmark for assessing market demand and procurement costs.

Headline: Chana Prices Strengthen Further, October Average Reaches ₹74,393/Tonne
Summary: Chana prices remained elevated on 13 October, with the Delhi market averaging ₹74,393/tonne, up from ₹59,181/tonne in October last year and ₹67,321/tonne in September 2026. The October average is approximately 25.7% higher year-on-year and 10.5% above September. Spot prices show a strong upward trend since late September, with Rajasthan-origin Chana in Delhi holding at ₹76,000/tonne and Bikaner FAQ at ₹74,000/tonne. However, the latest market data indicates selective corrections, including declines in Australian Chana in Mumbai and Desi Chana in Alwar and Sedam. Prices remain well above historical averages, although profit-booking and government stock releases may cause short-term volatility.

Headline: Tur Prices Remain Elevated Despite Profit-Booking in Major Markets
Summary: Tur prices averaged ₹96,286/tonne in Delhi during October 2026 up to the 13th, compared with ₹68,458/tonne in October last year and ₹87,286/tonne in September. This represents a 40.7% year-

Summary: Burmese Lemon Tur in Delhi fell ₹3,000/tonne to ₹99,000, Vidarbha Tur in Akola declined ₹2,000 to ₹1,09,000, and Red Tur in Amravati dropped ₹5,000 to ₹1,05,000. Indore FAQ Tur gained ₹5,000 to ₹1,10,000, while most other markets remained stable or recorded modest changes. Tur prices remain well above historical averages, although profit-booking is creating short-term volatility.

Headline: Urad Prices Rise Sharply Year-on-Year Despite Mixed Spot Trends
Summary: Urad prices at Chennai averaged ₹93,429/tonne during October 1–13, 2026, compared with ₹67,400/tonne in October last year and ₹86,816/tonne in September. This represents a 38.6% year-on-year

Summary: Chennai FAQ held at ₹96,000/tonne, while Delhi FAQ declined ₹2,000 to ₹99,000 and Chennai Urad SQ fell ₹2,000 to ₹1,00,000. In contrast, Indore FAQ gained ₹5,000 to ₹1,01,000, while most other markets remained stable. Despite short-term corrections, Urad prices remain well above last year's levels, reflecting a firm overall market trend.

Headline: 76,300 Tonnes of Canadian Peas Expected at Mundra Port
Summary: A vessel carrying 76,300 tonnes of Canadian yellow peas is expected to arrive at Mundra Port on 13 October 2026, according to shipping agency reports. The shipment will add to India’s imported yellow pea availability and may support near-term supplies for millers and traders.

Headline: Cumin Prices Rise on Tight Supplies and Lower Production Outlook
Summary: Cumin futures settled 0.58% higher at ₹25,200, supported by tightening supplies of premium-quality seeds, lower arrivals across major markets and expectations of reduced production in the upcoming season. Farmers are holding stocks in anticipation of better prices during the October sowing period, while declining arrivals in Unjha and Rajasthan have strengthened near-term supply concerns. However, gains were limited by farmer selling ahead of the new season, rising NCDEX warehouse stocks and cautious industrial demand. Export demand from Europe and North America has improved for high-quality, residue-compliant cumin, although geopolitical tensions in the Middle East continue to disrupt logistics and traditional export markets. India’s cumin production is estimated at 90–92 lakh bags, down from 1.10 crore bags last year, including 42–45 lakh bags in Gujarat and 48–50 lakh bags in Rajasthan. Globally, China’s production is estimated at 70,000–80,000 tonnes due to adverse weather conditions, while Syria, Turkey and Afghanistan are expected to produce 9,000–10,000 tonnes, 10,000–11,000 tonnes and 10,000–12,000 tonnes, respectively.

Headline: Drought Conditions in Andhra Pradesh Raise Concerns Over Maize Production
Summary: Andhra Pradesh is facing severe drought conditions following a 53% rainfall deficit during June–August, with 388 of 688 mandals declared drought-hit. The deficient rainfall has raised concerns over crop growth and maize yields, increasing the risk of lower production and tighter supplies in the coming months. Reduced maize availability could put upward pressure on prices and increase procurement costs for poultry feed and ethanol industries.

Headline: USDA Raises US Corn Use for Ethanol to 5.7 Billion Bushels in 2026-27
Summary: The USDA has raised its forecast for US corn use in ethanol production for the 2026-27 marketing year to 5.7 billion bushels, up from 5.6 billion bushels projected in September. US corn production is forecast at 16.0 billion bushels, while total consumption is expected to reach 16.3 billion bushels. However, rising supplies are expected to outpace demand growth, pushing projected ending stocks up to 1.8 billion bushels. Reflecting the ample supply outlook, the USDA lowered its forecast for the season-average price received by US corn farmers to $4.7 per bushel. Globally, corn ending stocks are projected at 280.4 million tonnes, an increase of 8.3 million tonnes, largely due to higher US inventories.

Headline: Brazil Expands Corn Exports to China, Increasing Competition for US Suppliers
Summary: Brazil is strengthening its position in China’s corn market as shipments increase, while Argentina has also resumed commercial corn trade with China in 2026. China’s corn imports for 2026/27 are forecast at around 6.0 million tonnes, with US corn facing weaker price competitiveness compared with South American supplies. Stable Chinese feed demand is expected to intensify competition among exporters, with price competitiveness, tariff treatment and supply reliability likely to influence market share. Rising South American exports could put additional pressure on US corn exporters in the Chinese market.

Headline: Maharashtra’s Sugar Production Forecast Cut to 9.0 Million Tonnes for 2026-27
Summary: Maharashtra’s sugar production for the 2026-27 season has been revised downward to 9.0 million tonnes from the earlier estimate of 10.3 million tonnes, mainly due to deficient rainfall, higher temperatures and declining sugarcane quality. Sugarcane production is projected at 112.7 million tonnes across 1.54 million hectares, with an average yield of 74 tonnes per hectare and a sugar recovery rate of 9.5%. The state’s lower production outlook has raised concerns over sugar availability and prices in the upcoming season. However, the early commencement of crushing operations from October 15 is expected to help maintain domestic supplies during the festive period.

Headline: Government Tightens Sugar Stock Limits to Curb Hoarding
Summary: The Central Government has tightened sugar stockholding rules for traders, effective October 15, 2026, to curb hoarding and maintain market availability. Under the revised rules, traders can hold a maximum of 1,000 quintals of sugar for up to 15 days from the date of receipt, compared with the earlier limit of 2,000 quintals and 30 days. Kolkata and its extended metropolitan areas, along with Assam, will have a higher stock limit of 2,000 quintals. The revised order, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, is expected to improve stock monitoring and support stable sugar supplies in the domestic market.

Headline: Fiji Sugar Production Remains Below Previous Years Despite Improved Milling Efficiency
Summary: Fiji’s sugar production reached approximately 75,000 tonnes as of September 21, 2026, compared with 110,000 tonnes in 2025 and 180,000 tonnes in 2017. Sugarcane deliveries stood at around 760,000 tonnes during the current crushing season. Meanwhile, milling efficiency improved, with the Tonnes Cane to Tonnes Sugar (TCTS) ratio declining to 10.3 from 13.3 in 2025, indicating better sugar recovery. Cumulative sugar export earnings reached approximately $42 million up to July 2026, compared with $50 million for the whole of 2025. The long-term decline in sugarcane supply and sugar output highlights the challenges facing Fiji’s sugar industry, although full-year 2026 production figures are not yet available.

Headline: Nigeria Plans $7.1 Billion Investment to Achieve Sugar Self-Sufficiency
Summary: Nigeria plans to invest $7.1 billion over the next decade to increase annual sugar production to over 2 million metric tonnes, save $4.1 billion in foreign exchange and create around 110,000 jobs. The country currently depends heavily on imported raw sugar, with domestic production at approximately 27,000 tonnes annually. The programme focuses on expanding existing sugar mills, developing sugarcane farms and establishing 10 new sugar projects to reduce import dependence and strengthen the domestic sugar industry.

Headline: India’s Maize Inflation Rises to 0.37% in September 2026
Summary: According to the latest data, inflation in maize and its products in India increased to 0.37% in September 2026, compared with -0.09% in August. The inflation rate had declined to -2.89% in June before gradually recovering. The latest increase indicates a shift into positive inflation, reflecting a change in the price trend of maize and its products.

Headline: Coriander prices showed upward trend in the Gondal market as lower arrivals, whereas October NCDEX futures witnessed upward
Summary: Coriander prices at the Gondal market showed upward trend on 13th Oct. The Badami and Eagle Plus variety are quoted at 1,50,000, and 1,56,000 INR/tonne, varieties up by 2,000 INR each. On the National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange, coriander contract for October delivery inclined by Rs 202, or 1.30 per cent, to Rs 15,716 per quintal with an open interest of 6,675 lots. In last week (till 10th Oct), cumulative arrivals during the current market year (April to March) reached 1,55,769 tonnes, representing a 30.7% decline compared to the same period last year. Meanwhile, Total stocks position at the Gondal and Kota markets currently stand at 12,838 tonnes, of Unencumbered Valid Stock, Pledged Valid Stock, and Quantity in Process, whereas Unencumbered Valid Stock accounts for 5,721 tonnes.

Headline: Gujarat Coriander Arrivals Remain Steady as NCDEX December Futures Decline
Summary: Gujarat's major agricultural markets recorded coriander arrivals on October 13, 2026, with Gondal leading at around 900 bags, followed by Junagadh at 600 bags and Rajkot at 200 bags. Other mandis reported arrivals of approximately 100–150 bags. The NCDEX December coriander contract declined by ₹128 to ₹16,182, indicating a weaker trend in futures trading.

Headline: Cumin Prices remain unchanged in Unjha market while decline in Oct NCDEX Futures and higher Arrivals
Summary: Cumin prices at the Unjha market remain unchanged on 13th Oct. The FAQ and Machine Cleaned variety quoted at 2,35,000 and 2,70,000 INR/Tonne. On the National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange, cumin contracts for Oct delivery downward by Rs 500, or 0.68 per cent, to Rs 25,640 per quintal with an open interest of 1,662 lots. In last week (till 10th Oct), cumulative arrivals during the current market year (April to March) reached 3,64,662 tonnes, representing a 21.3% incline compared to the same period last year. NCDEX Total stocks position at the Unjha market currently stand at 3,083 tonnes, of Unencumbered Valid Stock, and Pledged Valid Stock, meanwhile Unencumbered Valid Stock accounts for 2,269 tonnes.

Headline: Ethanol Demand and Weak Monsoon Push Up Poultry Feed Costs
Summary: India’s rising ethanol demand and weak monsoon conditions are tightening maize supplies and increasing poultry feed costs. Maize prices paid by poultry farmers rose to ₹27–28 per kg in late September, compared with ₹12–14 in 2019. Karnataka’s maize production is estimated to have declined by 25% this season due to drought-related crop damage. Higher procurement costs have pushed meat retailers to increase chicken prices, while rising feed expenses are also adding to household food costs.

Headline: Turmeric Prices showed upward trend in Nizamabad Market, incline October NCDEX Futures and Arrivals Surge
Summary: Turmeric prices at the Nizamabad market showed upward trend on 13th Oct. Finger, Gattah and Nizam varieties quoted at 2,25,000, 1,95,000, and 1,10,000 INR/tonne, Gattah variety up by 5,000 INR. On the National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange, coriander contracts for October delivery up by Rs 160, or 0.65 per cent, to Rs 24,686 per quintal with an open interest of 6,920 lots. In last week (till 10th Oct), cumulative arrivals during the current market year (Jan to Dec) reached 4,61,127 tonnes, representing a 121.6% Incline compared to the same period last year. Total stocks position at the Basmat, Erode, Nizamabad, and Sangli markets currently stand at 21,832 tonnes, of Unencumbered Valid Stock, Pledged Valid Stock, and Quantity in Process, meanwhile Unencumbered Valid Stock accounts for 17,684 tonnes.

Headline: Turmeric Prices Rise due to Karnataka Drought Concerns
Summary: Turmeric futures settled 0.19% higher at ₹22,332, supported by drought-related crop damage in Karnataka. A joint survey estimated losses across 13,446 hectares, against total state cultivation of around 18,000-20,000 hectares. Tight supplies, concerns over El Niño and declining carry-forward stocks, estimated at around 15 lakh bags against over 20 lakh bags last season, further supported prices. However, renewed monsoon activity across Maharashtra, Telangana and North Karnataka, along with improved reservoir levels in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, has eased immediate weather concerns.

Headline: Chilli Prices remain unchanged at Guntur Market; higher Arrivals
Summary: Chilli prices at the Guntur market remain unchanged on 13th Oct. Bedki, LCA 334 - loose, No. 273, No.5/ fatki, Sannam, and Teja varieties quoted at 2,75,000, 2,80,000, 2,60,000, 2,55,000, 2,85,000 and 2,20,000 INR/tonne, No. 273 and Teja variety up by 5,000 INR each. In last week (till 10th Oct), cumulative arrivals during the current market year (Mar to Feb) reached 7,52,028 tonnes representing a 32.4 incline compared to the same period last year.

Headline: Unseasonal Rain in Punjab Threatens Paddy Stocks but Wheat Sowing Expected to Remain on Track
Summary: Unseasonal rainfall in Punjab has raised concerns over standing paddy crops and harvested grain lying in open mandis, with further rain, thunderstorms and strong winds forecast for October 13–15 under a yellow alert. Farmers have been advised to protect mature paddy and cover market stocks to minimise quality losses. Delayed government procurement, which began on October 1 compared with September 16 last year, has increased exposure of paddy stored in mandis to adverse weather. However, agricultural experts expect that a short delay in paddy harvesting will have limited impact on wheat sowing, as the main planting period begins in November.

Headline: Flooding in Uttar Pradesh’s Basti District Damages 70% of Bethauha Farmers’ Crops, Threatens Wheat Sowing
Summary: Flooding of the Kuano River has submerged paddy fields in Bethauha village in Bhanpur tehsil, with nearly 70% of the village’s farmers reportedly suffering crop losses. Around 250 farmers cultivate land in the village, much of it in low-lying areas where prolonged waterlogging has damaged paddy crops. Farmers warned that delayed drainage could disrupt the upcoming wheat sowing season and cause further losses. They also alleged that crop damage assessments had been delayed and sought compensation. The district administration has formed a joint revenue and agriculture department team to assess flood-related crop losses.

Headline: India’s Rice Prices Rise 10–25% as Weak Monsoon Threatens Production and Exports
Summary: India’s rice production is forecast to decline 4.5% to 147.0 MMT in 2026/27 from around 154.0 MMT in 2025/26, amid deficient rainfall, El Niño risks and reduced acreage. Kharif rice area fell 3.7% year-on-year to 42.9 million hectares, with declines reported in Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Average retail rice prices reached ₹46.9/kg, up around 10% year-on-year, while premium non-basmati varieties rose 10–25%. India’s rice exports are projected to fall 4% to 24.0 MMT in 2027, potentially tightening global supplies, as India accounts for over 40% of global rice exports. However, central rice stocks remain above 38.0 MMT against a buffer requirement of 10.25 MMT, providing scope for market releases to moderate domestic price pressures.

Headline: Tamil Nadu Fine Rice Prices Rise Amid Tight Supplies and Higher Costs
Summary: Fine and superfine rice prices in Tamil Nadu have increased sharply over the past 10 days, with a 26-kg bag of superfine rice rising to ₹1,950 from ₹1,720 and fine rice to ₹1,640 from ₹1,500. Higher paddy procurement prices, rising fertiliser and fuel costs, labour shortages, lower arrivals from other states and stronger urban demand have contributed to the increase. Government paddy procurement reached a record 6.4 MMT in 2025/26, up from 4.8 MMT in the previous season, reducing supplies available to private buyers. Tamil Nadu consumes around 9.1 MMT of rice annually but produces only 7.0–7.5 MMT locally, relying on other states for the balance. Industry representatives said there is no overall rice shortage and expect supplies to improve after the Samba harvest concludes in January 2027.

Headline: Interstate Traders Offer ₹4,000–₹4,600 per Quintal for Telangana Paddy Amid Rising Rice Prices
Summary: Private traders from Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu are purchasing paddy directly from farmers in Telangana, offering ₹4,000–₹4,600 per quintal against the government MSP of ₹2,440–₹2,460. Purchases are underway in Nizamabad, Karimnagar, Khammam and Rangareddy districts, with some traders providing advance payments to secure supplies before harvesting is complete. The government has also announced a ₹500/quintal bonus for seven fine rice varieties, but private offers remain substantially higher. Meanwhile, Hyderabad retail prices for fine rice have climbed to ₹85–₹90/kg, with a 25-kg bag rising by ₹300–₹400 over the past 30–45 days. Increased private procurement and expectations of further price gains could tighten local paddy availability and add to retail price pressures.

Headline: Uttar Pradesh Sets 6.5 MMT Paddy Procurement Target for KMS 2026/27, Promises Payments Within 48 Hours
Summary: Uttar Pradesh has set a paddy procurement target of 6.5 MMT for the 2026/27 Kharif marketing season, up from the record 6.2 MMT procured in the previous season, with purchases planned through 4,500 centres operated by eight government agencies. Procurement will run from October 15, 2026, to February 15, 2027, in western UP and from November 1, 2026, to February 28, 2027, in eastern UP. The minimum support price is ₹2,441/quintal for common-grade paddy and ₹2,461/quintal for Grade A.

Headline: Bangladesh Rice Prices Rise as Higher Fuel and Paddy Costs Increase Market Expenses
Summary: Rice prices increased across several districts of Bangladesh, including Dhaka, over the past week as higher transport costs, rising paddy prices, and seasonal supply factors pushed up prices. Fine rice in Dhaka retail markets rose to Tk 74–75/kg from Tk 72, while medium-grain rice increased to Tk 58–65/kg from Tk 55–62; coarse rice remained at Tk 50–55/kg. Transport costs for a truckload of rice from Kushtia to Dhaka increased 20% to Tk 24,000 from Tk 20,000 following a Tk 20/litre fuel price hike. Paddy prices in producing areas rose to Tk 1,240 per maund from Tk 1,120 over the past month, while mill-gate fine rice prices reached Tk 55–67/kg. However, official market data showed mixed trends, with authorities reviewing discrepancies between reported retail prices and government figures.

Headline: Pakistan Offers to Supply the Philippines 1.0 MMT of Rice Annually
Summary: Pakistan is seeking to expand rice exports to the Philippines, offering to supply at least 1.0 MMT annually subject to mutually agreed commercial terms. The proposal was presented at the International World Rice Conference 2026 in Manila, held from October 7–9, with more than 20 Pakistani companies participating. Pakistan exported around 300,000 tonnes of rice worth $117 million to the Philippines during July–September 2026, with rice accounting for 75% of its total exports to the country. Trade discussions focused on procurement requirements, product specifications, pricing, and long-term supply arrangements, as Pakistan looks to strengthen its position in the Philippine rice market and support the country’s food security.
